agentCan: Implement the OAuth 1.0a HMAC-SHA256 signing for PaaS integration calls (and the handshake endpoints where used)
Implement the IMS client_credentials / authorization-code flows for SaaS stores
Detect each merchant's deployment flavor and route to the right stack

approval.cost: No review timeline or listing fee for Commerce Marketplace is stated in the pages read; SaaS license/Developer Console pricing also not stated
approval.trigger: No Adobe review or approval exists for connecting a store, in either flavor. For PaaS, the only authorization is the merchant's own: 'Merchants authorize extensions and applications to access or update store data' by creating the integration in their Admin and clicking 'Allow' on the activation pop-up ('A pop-up window displays, confirming API permissions. Click Allow.'). There is no Adobe-side gate, waitlist, or per-app approval, and no pre-approval caps; access is bounded only by the ACL resources the merchant grants the integration (all resources, or a customized subset). SaaS gating is entitlement-based, not review-based: prerequisites are an Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service license and Adobe Developer Console access (and an Adobe Organization Admin account for server-to-server setup); no review step or timeline is described. Optional, separate distribution: listing an app/extension on Commerce Marketplace DOES require review (the Extension Quality Program: technical review begins with package upload, malware scan and package verification plus coding-standard checks; marketing review covers listing content), but this is only for Marketplace distribution, not for connecting to a merchant's store.
approval.wait: None for connections (no review exists); Marketplace review duration not stated

blockers.detail: 'The traditional admin and integration token generation methods is not supported in SaaS environments. Instead, you must obtain an IMS admin token through OAuth authentication.' A vendor must detect each merchant's deployment flavor and support both OAuth 1.0a integrations (PaaS) and IMS OAuth 2 (SaaS); neither flow works on the other.
blockers.howToClear: Build flavor detection into onboarding and maintain both auth stacks.
blockers.title: Two incompatible stacks (one-way door by deployment type)

blockers.detail: Onboarding is a manual, per-store procedure inside each merchant's Admin (create integration, grant resources, activate, Allow), and credentials are unique per store. There is no central app record a merchant can simply approve.
blockers.howToClear: Ship merchant-facing, step-by-step Admin instructions and a secure credential intake.
blockers.title: No one-click connect for PaaS

blockers.detail: Using the integration access token on its own as a Bearer token 'has been disabled by default due to the security implications of a never-expiring access token. Namely, if the access token is compromised it provides undetected persistent access to a store.' It can be re-enabled (Admin setting or CLI bin/magento config:set oauth/consumer/enable_integration_as_bearer), but Adobe recommends signing requests with all four credentials instead.
blockers.howToClear: Sign every request with the full OAuth 1.0a credential set; do not depend on the bearer shortcut.
blockers.title: Standalone-bearer trap

alternatives: Admin token (a merchant admin's username/password, plus mandatory two-factor authentication, exchanged for a Bearer token; acts as that admin; default validity 4 hours, configurable)
Customer token (customer username/password; only anonymous/self resources; default lifetime 1 hour)
Guest/anonymous access (no auth; anonymous resources only)
IMS access tokens for PaaS web API calls when the Commerce Admin is integrated with IMS (life set by IMS, default 24 hours)
flavor.recommended: PaaS: an Integration using OAuth 1.0a authentication, created in each merchant's store Admin. SaaS: your Developer Console project with IMS OAuth 2 (server-to-server, or user authentication when calls must run as a specific admin)
flavor.why: Adobe Commerce has two deployment flavors with completely different auth stacks. (A) PaaS (Adobe Commerce on cloud infrastructure, on-premises, Magento Open Source): 'In Commerce, a third-party application that uses OAuth for authentication is called an integration. An integration defines which resources the application can access. The application can be granted access to all resources or a customized subset of resources.' The Integration is created inside each merchant's own store Admin (System > Extensions > Integrations); activation generates four credentials (consumer key, consumer secret, access token, access token secret). Two activation variants: self-activated ('After activating an integration (self activated), you can use the generated consumer key, consumer secret, access token, and access token secret to provide third-party systems access... You do not need to make calls to the /oauth/token/request or /oauth/token/access endpoints'), or the full handshake (you supply Callback URL and Identity Link URL; Commerce POSTs the credentials and an oauth_verifier to your endpoint; your app completes the 2-legged OAuth 1.0a exchange). (B) SaaS (Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service): an Adobe Developer Console project with IMS OAuth credentials for the 'Adobe Commerce with Adobe ID' API (OAuth Server-to-Server technical account, or User Authentication via OAuth Web App / SPA / Native App); required scopes include commerce.accs plus AdobeID, openid, email, profile, additional_info.roles, additional_info.projectedProductContext. Integration/admin tokens are explicitly NOT supported in SaaS.

humanMust: (Merchant admin, PaaS) Create and activate the Integration in their store Admin, granting API resources, and hand over the four credentials (self-activated) or complete the handshake activation
(Org admin/developer, SaaS) Create the Developer Console project and complete the Server Authentication setup (requires an Adobe Organization Admin account)
name: Adobe Commerce (Magento)
nuances: Token figures (provider-stated): Integration access tokens are 'Indefinite. It lasts until it is manually revoked' ('Access tokens are long-lived and will not expire unless the merchant revokes access from the application'). Admin tokens default to 4 hours (configurable under Stores > Configuration > Services > OAuth > Access Token Expiration; an hourly cron removes expired tokens); customer tokens default to 1 hour; IMS access tokens on PaaS default to 24 hours; the SaaS user-auth example response shows expires_in 86399 (about 24 hours), and the server-to-server guide uses whatever expires_in IMS returns.

Merchant-controlled scope: the integration's resources are chosen by the merchant from the ACL tree at creation. If a needed resource isn't granted, calls fail, and expanding access requires the merchant to change the integration in their Admin; it cannot be requested or widened via the API. Revocation is entirely merchant-side: because tokens never expire, the connection lives until the merchant manually revokes/deactivates the integration.
Signing burden: every handshake and API request must carry a correctly constructed HMAC-SHA256 OAuth 1.0a signature (signing key = consumer secret + '&' + token secret) in the Authorization header.

SaaS header rigidity: the commerce.accs scope must be included in token generation, and server-to-server API calls require the x-api-key (Client ID) and x-gw-ims-org-id (Organization ID) headers in addition to the Bearer token, per the guide's client example.
prerequisites: Per-merchant: a store Admin willing to create the Integration (PaaS) or an Adobe Organization Admin for the Console project (SaaS)
Secure storage for the per-store four-credential set (PaaS)
For the handshake variant: a callback endpoint and an identity-link login page on your service

steps.detail: In your service, build a callback endpoint and an identity-link login page (handshake variant). The merchant goes to System > Extensions > Integrations > Add New Integration, enters Name, Callback URL, Identity Link URL, and selects API resources on the API tab (the ACL tree: 'All' or a custom subset).
steps.title: (PaaS) Merchant creates the Integration

steps.detail: Merchant clicks Save and Activate (or Activate on a saved integration) and clicks 'Allow' on the permissions confirmation pop-up. Self-activated: Commerce generates the access token/secret directly and the merchant copies all four credentials to you out of band. Handshake: Commerce POSTs store_base_url, oauth_verifier, oauth_consumer_key, oauth_consumer_secret to your callback URL; the merchant logs in to your app via the identity link; your app calls POST /oauth/token/request then POST /oauth/token/access (with the verifier), signed per OAuth 1.0a (HMAC-SHA256), and receives the access token + secret.
steps.title: (PaaS) Activate; receive the credentials

steps.detail: Sign every API call with all four credentials in the Authorization header (OAuth 1.0a, HMAC-SHA256). Tokens never expire; the connection lives until the merchant revokes the integration.
steps.title: (PaaS) Call the API with signed requests

steps.detail: Create/select a project in Adobe Developer Console and complete the Server Authentication setup (prerequisites: Developer Console access and an Adobe Organization Admin account); note Client ID, Client Secret, Organization ID. POST ims-na1.adobelogin.com/ims/token/v3 with grant_type=client_credentials and the scope string including commerce.accs; cache the token until its expires_in. Call the REST API with Authorization: Bearer, plus x-api-key: <Client ID> and x-gw-ims-org-id: <Organization ID>.
steps.title: (SaaS) Server-to-server via IMS

steps.detail: In Developer Console, create a project, add the Adobe Commerce with Adobe ID API, choose OAuth Web App / SPA / Native App, configure redirect URIs, copy Client ID and Client Secret. Redirect the merchant's admin user to ims-na1.adobelogin.com/ims/authorize/v2 (response_type=code, full scope set); exchange the code at POST /ims/token/v3 (Basic auth, grant_type=authorization_code); the response includes access_token, refresh_token, and id_token.
steps.title: (SaaS) User authentication variant

tagline: Two products wearing one name: PaaS stores connect through a merchant-created Integration with OAuth 1.0a credentials that never expire, while Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service uses IMS OAuth 2 from the Adobe Developer Console, and the two stacks do not interoperate. No Adobe review gates either connection; only Marketplace listing is reviewed.

time.active: ~15 min of merchant-admin setup per store + ~half a day of signing/flow code
time.total: Same day per store; no Adobe wait
